purpose: Prepare a qualified gravitational-wave reviewer to make bounded scientific judgments without treating machine checks as scientific validation.

sources.title: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger
sources.authors: B. P. Abbott et al. (LIGO Scientific Collaboration and Virgo Collaboration)
supports: The published visualization uses a 35-350 Hz bandpass plus line-rejection filters.
GW150914 is visible over approximately 0.2 s, increasing from about 35 to 150 Hz.
The observed L1-to-H1 delay is approximately 6.9 ms and occurs within the 10 ms intersite propagation time.
The published visual alignment shifts and inverts one detector because of relative detector orientations.
sources.does_not_support: It does not validate this packet's bandpass-only, unwhitened, unnotched correlation statistic, exact 820-sample window, 0.30 threshold, or use of the maximum absolute correlation.

sources.title: Data Release for Event GW150914
sources.locator: Version 2 event page and 4096 Hz H1/L1 strain files
supports: Dataset identity, event time, public access, and CC BY 4.0 status.
Version 2 corrects a phase error in the earlier 4 kHz files.
sources.does_not_support: The release does not independently validate the local processing choices or result.

sources.title: Technical details for Advanced LIGO and Virgo event data releases
sources.locator: Data quality for event data release; Injections for the event data releases
supports: DATA records availability; CAT1, CAT2, and CAT3 identify increasingly broader categories of known data-quality concern.
A set injection bit means that the named class of hardware injection is absent.
sources.does_not_support: Passing the public bit fields is not a fresh detector-characterization investigation, calibration audit, or proof that no unmodeled noise is present.

sources.title: The O1 Data Release
supports: Quality categories are analysis-group specific and cumulative within a group.
GWOSC identifies DATA, CBC_CAT1, and CBC_CAT2 as the general floor for binary-black-hole search use.
sources.does_not_support: It does not establish that this case's combined CBC and burst flag policy is uniquely correct for a correlation demonstration.

sources.title: A guide to LIGO-Virgo detector noise and extraction of transient gravitational-wave signals
sources.authors: B. P. Abbott et al. (LIGO Scientific Collaboration and Virgo Collaboration)
supports: An LVC worked visualization uses a zero-phase eighth-order 35-350 Hz Butterworth bandpass after windowing and whitening, and explicitly limits that narrow bandpass to visualization rather than parameter estimation.

GW150914 correlation results depend materially on the chosen bandpass and time window; the paper compares 0.2 s, 0.1 s, and 0.04 s windows and records an anti-correlation near the expected delay under its convention.
Correlation timing is a bounded consistency diagnostic and requires a specified statistic, background, and broader detector-validation context for stronger inference.
sources.does_not_support: It does not validate this packet's fourth-order direct-to-strain filter, omission of whitening/window taper/notches, exact window centering, maximum-absolute-correlation rule, or 0.30 threshold.

sources.title: Characterization of transient noise in Advanced LIGO relevant to gravitational wave signal GW150914
sources.authors: B. P. Abbott et al. (LIGO Scientific Collaboration and Virgo Collaboration)
supports: Data-quality vetoes are search- and detector-specific and materially affect transient backgrounds.
The published scientific assessment used detector-characterization and environmental checks beyond public event-time flags.
sources.does_not_support: The packet does not reproduce those background, environmental, or detector-characterization studies.

machine_observations.statement: The exact registered GWOSC-v2 H1 and L1 files pass content, version, geometry, and finite-value checks.
At the selected event second, DATA, CBC_CAT1, CBC_CAT2, BURST_CAT1, and BURST_CAT2 are set and NO_CBC_HW_INJ and NO_BURST_HW_INJ are set for both detectors.
The registered 35-350 Hz fourth-order forward-backward Butterworth path and 820-sample window recover lag 5.37109375 ms and correlation -0.400196295324 by maximizing absolute normalized correlation.
A zero-padded +25 ms L1-window shift produces an absolute lag of 19.53125 ms and fails the registered 10 ms necessary-bound decision.

required_human_determinations.question: Is the 35-350 Hz forward-backward Butterworth filter, without whitening or notch filters, acceptable for this bounded demonstration, and are its differences from the published visualization sufficiently explicit?
Is the exact 820-sample window centered at GPS 1126259462.4 an adequate and non-misleading choice for this bounded lag demonstration?
Does the event-time DATA/CBC/BURST and transient-injection policy support only the stated preprocessing scope, with detector characterization and calibration still accepted externally?
Are lag sign, detector-orientation inversion, and maximum-absolute-correlation conventions disclosed well enough to prevent the negative correlation from being overinterpreted?

Is 10 ms used strictly as a necessary geometric bound rather than evidence of astrophysical origin, and is the 0.30 correlation floor correctly labeled as a registered local threshold rather than a literature-derived detection criterion?
Are the accepted upstream calibration, event curation, detector-state metadata, library, and platform boundaries and all unwarranted conclusions complete for the strongest stated conclusion?

strongest_candidate_conclusion: bounded computational repeatability of the registered processing path and satisfaction of one necessary intersite-lag invariant
conclusions_not_available_from_this_revi: reproduction of the original search or detection significance
proof that the correlation is astrophysical
integrity_rule: The prepared dossier may be machine-checked for completeness, but only a named qualified human can supply the scientific disposition.
